correctness.rationale: The full three-dimensional Jacobian has eigenvalues cos(u)-b and -b-cos(u)/2±i(sqrt(3)/2)cos(u), exactly determining a hyperbolic sink. On each positive sine lobe, g(u)=sin(u)/u rises then falls for k>=1, with unique turning point tan(u)=u; the k=0 lobe decreases. Only the descending root can be a sink, and the additional strict inequality cos(u)>-2g(u) changes at the unique root tan(u)=-u/2 on the right half-lobe. Disjointness follows from a strict denominator inequality for adjacent endpoints. Uniform cotangent expansions yield F_k-H_k=(9/2)v_k^-3+O(v_k^-5); integral comparison at spacing 2pi gives |S∩(0,epsilon)|=9epsilon²/(8pi)+O(epsilon³), with at most one partial window. Separately executed numerical checks support root identities; they are not used to prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The natural question is whether the nontrivial synchronous stationary states of the archetypal Thomas sine-feedback flow are full-dimensional sinks at a given damping. The theorem gives a complete answer for every positive damping, not a single parameter or special solution. The coexistence of infinitely many disjoint stable windows accumulating at vanishing damping with a sharp quadratic vanishing-density law is a structurally meaningful and quantifiable bifurcation hierarchy, and the measure constant distinguishes this system from a generic example or routine Jacobian computation.
